reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected GAAP rows shows revenue rising while total expenses were nearly flat, so operating income, pretax income, net income and diluted EPS all rose on the same basis. The operating-income increase is arithmetically consistent with the revenue increase outpacing the expense increase, and the expense line itself is mixed: cost of revenue rose while research and development and selling, general and administrative declined. The tax provision rose alongside pretax income, so the after-tax improvement is not attributable to a lower tax burden; the tax line is a same-direction subtotal and is not opposing evidence. The thesis is a source-bounded baseline with no valuation, catalyst or invalidation conditions, so the selected rows neither confirm nor refute a specific assumption; the appropriate research state is to maintain the thesis at unchanged conviction while recording the new source. Material counterevidence is limited to the rising cost of revenue and the higher tax provision, which indicate that not all of the profit improvement flowed through and that the after-tax gain was partly absorbed by tax. Uncertainty is substantial: these are selected displayed rows rather than complete filings, the comparison is sequential rather than year-over-year, no non-GAAP or company-defined measures, guidance, segment detail, backlog, margin percentages or share-count data are in the extract, and no causal driver is established. Evidence that would change the view includes full-filing segment and recurring-revenue detail, company guidance versus realized results, non-GAAP reconciliations, and year-over-year comparatives.
